title: Quant triage + daily runlog
content:
Daily scratchpad — quick log + triage notes

2026-03-10 (start) -> 2026-03-12 (last touch)
Owner: Violet Park (working solo this morning; pinged Arjun + Maya on anomalies)

Top-level objective:
- Find minimal quant config that meets latency SLO (p99 < 250ms for 512 tokens, batch=1) while keeping generation quality drop < 3% on our instruction eval set.
- Investigate weird KV-cache blowup when using grouped-quantize (per-channel) + continous-batch on A100s.

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: per-channel 3-bit (GPTQ-style) with outlier handling disabled causes larger KV deltas per layer -> increases KV write traffic -> memory pressure and page thrashing on multi-tenant nodes.
- Hypothesis B: kernel selection fallback path on driver 535.x leads to slower matmul for small seq lengths in some layers; shows up only when quantized and batching enabled.
- Hypothesis C: prompt templates with long prefix tokens expose a cold-KV miss pattern that our cache-alignment optimization doesn't handle.

Immediate TODO (today):
- [ ] Re-run failing PR tests (quantization/pull/842) with driver 535.54 and 535.70 (compare).
- [ ] Add a KV mem profiler snapshot before/after generation for the short prefix case (scripts/kv_snapshot.py).
- [ ] Run small-grid: qc=3bit-per-channel (w/absmax outlier clamp, no group), qc=4bit-nt (per-tensor), qc=4bit-ptq with blocksize=64; models: rwd-13b-v0, rwd-7b-v1.
- [ ] Collect evals: instr-100 (our short instruction set), longform-20, reasoning-50.

Quick run plan / commands:
- docker run --gpus all --rm -e MODEL=rwd-13b-v0 -v $PWD:/work rwd-inference/quant-test:canary bash -c "python run_quant_eval.py --qc 3pc --batch 1 --seq 512 --out /work/out/3pc-13b.json"
- ./tools/kv_snapshot.py --pid $PID --out=kv-before.json  # capture pointers/sizes
- python perf/compare_kernels.py --logdir /var/log/runs/842 --driver 535.70

Observed failures / notes from yesterday's runs:
- run-2026-03-09-19:32: rwd-13b 3bit-pc produced occasional spikes in p99 (one sample at 1.2s) — stack trace shows fallback to torch.sparse_mm in attention_kv.py line ~438.
- Memory snapshot: KV table size jumped by ~12% between token 34 and 38 for same prompt; suspect additional temporary buffers allocated when zeroing quant scale arrays.
- Reproducer: prompt with system prefix (user: "Summarize this..." + 128 tokens of context) seems to trigger the spike consistently. Short prompts (<20 tokens) do not reproduce.

Preliminary numbers (very noisy) — baseline = fp16
- rwd-13b-v0 fp16: p50=85ms, p95=160ms, p99=220ms (512 toks, batch=1)
- rwd-13b-v0 4bit-nt: p50=70ms, p95=140ms, p99=210ms; instr-100 quality ~ -1.4% delta
- rwd-13b-v0 3bit-pc: p50=62ms, p95=135ms, p99 spikes; instr-100 quality ~ -3.8% delta
Notes: quality computed as avg ROUGE-L/EM hybrid on instr-100 — need to graduate to human eval on the 12 worst outputs.

Prompt set (working, rotate seed 7):
- T1: "Explain like I'm five: <topic>" (short-explain)
- T2: "Given the user goal: <goal>, produce a step-by-step plan (no fluff)." (instruction-heavy)
- T3: long-context comprehension: combine 4 paragraphs and ask for synthesis (used to reproduce KV blowup)
- T4: reasoning chain: multi-hop question (reasoning-50)

Notes-to-self about mitigations to try:
- Option 1: disable grouped per-channel quantization in attention projection matrices only (keep FFN quantized) — might reduce dynamic edge-case allocations.
- Option 2: force kernel hint: fused_attention_fastpath=true for quantized models on A100; test perf and correctness.
- Option 3: implement a lazy KV allocation that pre-reserves max expected size for sequence length to avoid reallocations mid-generation. More invasive but likely stable.

Quick checklist for today's PR: quantization/pull/842
- [ ] Add driver-version matrix in CI (535.54, 535.70, 536.x)
- [ ] Add a kv-cache snapshot unit that runs a short generation and asserts no >5% dynamic allocation between tokens 0..64
- [ ] Add a regression test using the long-context prompt T3 (seeded) to fail-fast on memory spikes

Misc scribbles (ideas/half-baked):
- Could try combining 4-bit nt + adaptive outlier correction on top of only the top-2 attention layers — might get most perf wins cheaply.
- Consider a tiny per-request "quant-compatibility mode" that forces fallback to fp16 for attention when seq_len > 256 on old drivers. (Useful short-term.)

Humans to ping:
- Arjun R: kernel perf hints, help with driver matrix CI
- Maya C: eval/quality reviewer — allocate 2 humans for quick curation of top-12 failures
- Omar P: infra-side, look at node allocation and noisy neighbor hypothesis

Appendix: quick links/notes I scribbled while debugging:
- stack excerpt: attention_kv.py:438 -> sparse_mm fallback -> torch._sparse_reduce
- local shell history snippet: run_quant_eval.py --seed 7 --qc 3pc --kv-optimize off
- NOTE: if reproducer fails, try fc_layerwise_clamp=0.8 param

End of day (2026-03-12) rough status:
- Repro success: yes (T3 prompt + rwd-13b 3pc). Next: test mitigations (Option1, Option2).
- CI patch queued: PR 842 updated with kv-snapshot test (wip).
- Blocking: need infra to schedule a stable A100 node with driver 535.70 for a 6-hour regression run (pinged Omar).

Next steps (tomorrow):
- Run 24h regressions on rwd-13b and rwd-7b with config matrix and collect perf + quality deltas; triage any new spikes.
- Draft quick confluence note summarizing findings (link to add once draft is up).

Random TODOs (low-priority):
- Add small utility to diff kv binary dumps (python script idea)
- Check GPU cgroup mem settings on noisy nodes

-- violet
